name: agent-fs-tools-decisions
body:
Decision record for the `agent-fs-tools` change-set [with user — Approach A, not reopened].

PROBLEM. Code-writer implementer agents cannot delete/move/copy files in their owned surface: the core implementer grants only `rm src/*.rs`, each frontend implementer one or two `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` patterns, and there is no `mv`/`cp` grant at all — so a plan `deletes`/`renames` task is unimplementable.

DECISION (Approach A). Add a small suite of filesystem tools — `apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp` — installed by `apg init`, whose path argument is scoped with per-path glob permissions in each agent's permission block (the same glob mechanism as `edit`, worktree-mirrored). Scope is rm + mv + cp; the shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants are replaced by the scoped fs-tool grants.

NON-GOALS. (1) The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are NOT edited — they are consumer artifacts refreshed out-of-band with the installed release; this change-set authors `opencode-suite/**` (product source embedded via `include_str!`) and the binary's install registry only. (2) No change to the binary's node/edge mutation surface (`apg node rm` / `apg edge rm` mutate graph nodes, not files). (3) No git-integrated fs (`git rm` / `git mv`) — plain filesystem operations only.

PROPOSED PERMISSION SHAPE (the exact frontmatter the agent-builder should generate for a core implementer; per-subsystem implementers use their own owned globs). The current scalar-ish block (`rm src/*.rs: allow` under `bash:`) is replaced by a deny-by-default glob map per tool, mirrored under `apg/.worktrees/*/` per agent-builder rule 10:

  apg_rm:
    "*": deny
    "src/*.rs": allow
    "apg/.worktrees/*/src/*.rs": allow
  apg_mv:
    "*": deny
    "src/*.rs": allow
    "apg/.worktrees/*/src/*.rs": allow
  apg_cp:
    "*": deny
    "src/*.rs": allow
    "apg/.worktrees/*/src/*.rs": allow

and the `bash:` block drops its `rm src/*.rs` line (the fs tools supersede it). For a tool with two path arguments (mv/cp) both the source and the destination must match the granted globs.

OPEN QUESTION (flagged for review). Whether opencode applies a custom tool's permission block as per-argument path matching (the `edit` shape) or as a tool-level allow/deny. If it is tool-level only, the scoping enforcement must move inside the tool (path resolved against the caller's project directory and refused outside the acting role's granted surface) — see `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`'s FALLBACK clause. The observable acceptance (out-of-scope path refused) is unchanged either way.
